scope: A practical, source-backed catalog of the core crypto strategies, signals, and indicators explicitly covered by the cited guides. It is not literally every proprietary or newly invented method in existence.

strategies.name: HODLing
strategies.formula: No fixed trading formula; buy and hold the asset for the long term.
strategies.description: Passive long-term exposure rather than frequent trading.
strategies.useful_when: You have a long horizon and want to avoid short-term timing decisions.
strategies.not_useful_when: You need short-term income, cannot tolerate large drawdowns, or the asset thesis has failed.

strategies.name: Dollar-cost averaging (DCA)
strategies.formula: Amount per purchase = total budget / number of scheduled purchases.
strategies.description: Invest a fixed amount at regular intervals regardless of price.
strategies.useful_when: You want disciplined exposure, have regular income, and do not want to time the market.
strategies.not_useful_when: The asset trends down for a prolonged period, fees are high, or you need to exploit short-term opportunities.

strategies.name: Day trading
strategies.formula: Net P&L = position size × (exit price − entry price) − fees − funding/slippage.
strategies.description: Open and close positions within the same trading day using chart-based entries and exits.
strategies.useful_when: You can monitor markets actively and have liquid markets, tight execution, and a tested rule set.
strategies.not_useful_when: You cannot monitor positions, liquidity is poor, or fees and slippage consume the expected edge.

strategies.name: Swing trading
strategies.formula: Typical signal = breakout above resistance + confirmation from SMA, Fibonacci, volume, MACD, or RSI; exit on invalidation or weakening structure.
strategies.description: Hold trades for multi-day or multi-week price swings.
strategies.useful_when: You prefer fewer decisions and can hold through normal short-term volatility.
strategies.not_useful_when: Markets are highly news-driven, range-bound without clean swings, or you cannot manage overnight risk.

strategies.name: Trend trading
strategies.formula: Entry follows a confirmed directional trend; exit when lower highs, MACD reversal, or fading volume indicate weakening momentum.
strategies.description: Stay in a position while the market continues making trend-consistent structure.
strategies.useful_when: A persistent bull or bear trend exists and you can tolerate pullbacks.
strategies.not_useful_when: The market is choppy or mean-reverting, where repeated trend signals whipsaw.

strategies.name: Scalping
strategies.formula: Net P&L per trade = (exit price − entry price) × quantity − trading fees − spread − slippage.
strategies.description: Take many very short-duration trades, often lasting seconds or minutes, for small price changes.
strategies.useful_when: Execution is fast, spreads and fees are low, liquidity is deep, and you can monitor continuously.
strategies.not_useful_when: Execution is slow, spreads are wide, fees are high, or discipline breaks down under rapid decision-making.

strategies.name: Arbitrage
strategies.formula: Net arbitrage edge = sell price − buy price − exchange fees − transfer costs − spread − slippage.
strategies.description: Buy an asset where it is cheaper and sell it where it is more expensive.
strategies.useful_when: Price differences persist long enough, transfers or hedges are fast, and all-in costs are below the gap.
strategies.not_useful_when: Transfers are delayed, withdrawals are restricted, liquidity is thin, or fees eliminate the gap.

strategies.name: Event-driven trading
strategies.formula: Trade trigger = predefined event plus directional confirmation; expected value = probability-weighted gain − probability-weighted loss − costs.
strategies.description: Trade around scheduled or unexpected events that can move crypto prices.
strategies.useful_when: The event is material, its timing and likely transmission are understood, and risk is capped.
strategies.not_useful_when: The event is already priced in, outcomes are binary and gap risk is large, or liquidity disappears.

indicators_and_signals.name: Simple moving average (SMA)
indicators_and_signals.description: The mean closing price over a chosen lookback period.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: You need a simple trend filter, support/resistance reference, or crossover signal.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: A fast reversal is underway; it is lagging and can signal after much of the move has occurred.

indicators_and_signals.name: Exponential moving average (EMA)
indicators_and_signals.formula: EMA_t = alpha × Price_t + (1 − alpha) × EMA_(t−1), where alpha = 2/(n+1).
indicators_and_signals.description: A moving average that weights recent observations more heavily than older ones.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: You want a more responsive trend or crossover signal than an SMA.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: The market is noisy or range-bound, producing frequent false crossovers.

indicators_and_signals.name: Moving-average crossover / golden cross
indicators_and_signals.formula: Bullish signal when short-period MA crosses above long-period MA; bearish signal when it crosses below.
indicators_and_signals.description: A trend-following signal built from two moving averages.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: A sustained trend is developing and delayed confirmation is acceptable.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: The market is ranging or reverses quickly, because crossovers lag and whipsaw.

indicators_and_signals.name: Relative Strength Index (RSI)
indicators_and_signals.formula: RSI = 100 − 100/(1 + RS), where RS = average gain / average loss over n periods.
indicators_and_signals.description: A 0–100 momentum oscillator; Kraken identifies below 30 as oversold and above 70 as overbought.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: You are testing momentum exhaustion, divergences, or pullback entries with price-action confirmation.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: A strong trend keeps RSI overbought or oversold; standalone reversal trades can fail.

indicators_and_signals.name: Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD)
indicators_and_signals.formula: MACD = EMA(12) − EMA(26); signal line = EMA(9) of MACD; histogram = MACD − signal line.
indicators_and_signals.description: Momentum and trend indicator composed of a MACD line, signal line, and histogram.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: You want crossover, zero-line, histogram, or divergence confirmation of momentum shifts.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: The market is sideways or moves too quickly; lag and repeated crossovers can create false signals.

indicators_and_signals.name: Bollinger Bands
indicators_and_signals.formula: Middle = SMA(n); upper = middle + kσ; lower = middle − kσ (Kraken describes k=2 as the standard example).
indicators_and_signals.description: A middle moving average with upper and lower standard-deviation bands.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: You are assessing volatility contraction, breakout setups, or short-term mean reversion with confirmation.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: Price trends strongly along a band or a low-volume/wash-traded market makes band touches unreliable.

indicators_and_signals.name: Stochastic oscillator
indicators_and_signals.formula: %K = 100 × (Close − Lowest Low_n)/(Highest High_n − Lowest Low_n); %D = moving average of %K.
indicators_and_signals.description: Compares the close with its recent high-low range and oscillates from 0 to 100.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: You are timing pullbacks in a trend or looking for overbought/oversold crossovers and divergence.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: A strong trend keeps the oscillator extreme or the market is too noisy for clean crosses.

indicators_and_signals.name: On-Balance Volume (OBV)
indicators_and_signals.formula: OBV_t = OBV_(t−1) + volume_t if Close_t > Close_(t−1); OBV_(t−1) − volume_t if Close_t < Close_(t−1); unchanged if equal.
indicators_and_signals.description: A cumulative directional-volume measure used to compare volume flow with price action.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: You want volume confirmation or early divergence between price and buying/selling pressure.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: Reported volume is distorted by wash trading, fragmented venues, or illiquid markets.

indicators_and_signals.name: Fibonacci retracement
indicators_and_signals.formula: Retracement level = swing high − (swing high − swing low) × r, where r is commonly 0.236, 0.382, 0.50, or 0.618.
indicators_and_signals.description: Maps common percentage retracements between a selected swing high and swing low to estimate support/resistance.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: A clear swing exists and you need pullback zones or confluence with structure.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: Swing anchors are subjective, price is news-driven, or levels are treated as certainty rather than zones.

indicators_and_signals.name: Average True Range (ATR)
indicators_and_signals.formula: TR_t = max(high−low, |high−previous close|, |low−previous close|); ATR(n) = average of TR over n periods.
indicators_and_signals.description: A volatility measure based on true ranges.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: Setting volatility-scaled stops, targets, or position sizes.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: Used as a direction predictor; ATR measures movement magnitude, not whether price rises or falls.

indicators_and_signals.name: Percentage Price Oscillator (PPO)
indicators_and_signals.description: A MACD-like oscillator that expresses the difference between two EMAs as a percentage.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: Comparing momentum across assets with different price scales or confirming trend shifts.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: The market is choppy or the chosen EMAs are poorly matched to the trading horizon.

indicators_and_signals.name: Ichimoku Cloud
indicators_and_signals.formula: Tenkan = (9-period high + 9-period low)/2; Kijun = (26-period high + 26-period low)/2; Senkou A = (Tenkan + Kijun)/2 shifted forward; Senkou B = (52-period high + 52-period low)/2 shifted forward.
indicators_and_signals.description: A multi-line system for trend direction, momentum, and dynamic support/resistance; price above the cloud is described as bullish and below it as bearish.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: You want a multi-timeframe trend and level framework in a sustained market.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: The market is flat or highly volatile around the cloud, where signals overlap and whipsaw.

indicators_and_signals.name: VWAP
indicators_and_signals.formula: VWAP = Σ(price × volume) / Σ(volume) over the chosen session or window.
indicators_and_signals.description: Volume-weighted average price used by scalpers to identify short-term price/volume imbalance.
indicators_and_signals.useful_when: Intraday liquidity is adequate and you need an execution benchmark or mean-reversion reference.
indicators_and_signals.not_useful_when: The chosen session is arbitrary, volume is unreliable, or the market is making a strong one-way move.
